newsitem.title: FINLAND: GOVT TO SIT AS LONG AS HAS MAJORITY - LIPPONEN - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: GOVT TO SIT AS LONG AS HAS MAJORITY - LIPPONEN - PAPER.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says his government will remain in office as long as it has a majority in parliament, afternoon daily Iltalehti reported on Thursday.

Social Democratic Party chairman Lipponen, at the helm of a five-party left-right-green coalition since spring 1995, said his cabinet could stay on even if the Green Party and the Leftist Alliance opted out.
"Of course the government will continue (in office) ... both the EMU policy and the economic policy must stay on course," Lipponen was quoted as saying.
"As long as the government remains a majority government it will continue. There is no functioning alternative. The opposition in particular does not have one," he said.
Lipponen said he was not speculating in the potential future behaviour of any of the government parties.
Political observers have repeatedly said the Green Party and the Leftist Alliance may find it hard to go on supporting the cabinet's official pro-EMU stance.
The five government parties have 141 MPs in the 200 member single-chamber legislature. Without the Green Party and the Leftist Alliance, the coalition would control 113 seats.
